steps.title: Identify the noun’s case role
steps.body: In the supplied Муж говорит, the husband is the subject and the talking verb states its action. The subject noun is nominative. steps.title: Separate the subject from its description
steps.body: In Поезд старый, the train is the subject noun and old is its predicate description. This present property clause has no overt Russian copula. The noun’s case role is nominative subject, not accusative direct object. A dictionary-looking noun or familiar translation alone does not identify its role in every construction.

steps.title: Nouns that keep their form
steps.body: An indeclinable noun keeps the same form for case or number. In these examples, ра́дио and такси́ are indeclinable. Recognize the behavior of the shown noun.

steps.title: Four more unchanged nouns
steps.body: The nouns метро́, кино́, пальто́ and ко́фе are also indeclinable. Their forms stay unchanged for case or number. Learn the noun with this behavior; do not infer that every noun with a similar ending behaves the same way.

steps.title: Recognize the behavior

steps.title: Contrast nouns that can change
steps.body: Contrast кни́га and окно́: these nouns are declinable, so they can change for case. Their nominative and genitive forms differ. Choose the behavior of the shown noun: unchanged for case or number, or able to change for case. No new form needs to be invented.

steps.title: Review noun behavior
steps.body:
An indeclinable noun keeps the same form for case or number. In these examples, ра́дио and такси́ are indeclinable. Recognize the behavior of the shown noun.

The nouns метро́, кино́, пальто́ and ко́фе are also indeclinable. Their forms stay unchanged for case or number. Learn the noun with this behavior; do not infer that every noun with a similar ending behaves the same way.

кафе́ and меню́ are two more indeclinable nouns. An unchanged word form does not mean that a sentence has no case relationships. These checks classify the shown noun; they do not test production of a sentence or a complete paradigm.

Contrast кни́га and окно́: these nouns are declinable, so they can change for case. Their nominative and genitive forms differ. Choose the behavior of the shown noun: unchanged for case or number, or able to change for case. No new form needs to be invented.

steps.title: Possession versus absence
steps.body: A simple positive possession line places the possessed thing in the nominative. An absence line places the absent thing in the genitive. Decide whether the whole shown line affirms or denies possession.

steps.title: Positive statements and questions
steps.body: The son examples keep the same simple possession pattern in a statement or question: genitive possessor and nominative possessed thing. The form of a question does not turn the noun into an absence construction. Да, у меня есть сын. — Yes, I have a son. У твоего́ му́жа есть оди́н друг — Your husband has one friend.

steps.title: Keep quantity and absence separate
steps.body: The many-friends example includes a quantity expression. Quantity patterns are separate from the simple nominative possessed thing in the son checks. The no-son example below denies possession and uses the genitive for the absent thing. У моего нового мужа есть много друзе́й — My new husband has many friends. У меня́ нет сы́на — No, I don't have a son.
